newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Guangzhou Ship vows to control costs.
newsitem.headline: Guangzhou Ship vows to control costs.

text.p: Lower export tax rebates and unfavourable shipbuilding prices caused Guangzhou Shipyard International Co Ltd's 1996 net profit to fall 67 percent from the previous year, the company said on Monday.

"We will strengthen our internal management structuure, reduce our operational costs, as well as to increase our cost effectiveness in order to stay competitive," Hu Guoliang, chairman and general manager said in a statement.
The tax rebate on exported products fell to nine percent in 1996 from 15 percent, the company said. It also blamed a decline in container output and prices for lower net profits.
Guangzhou Shipyard last week said net profit for the year to December 31 was 33.30 million yuan against 101.28 million yuan in 1995.
Its 1995 accounts incorporated a 30.28 million yuan foreign exchange gain, but there was no such gain in 1996, it said.
However, Guangzhou Shipyard, which has an A-share listing in Shanghai and an H-share listing on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong, said its core business was increasing.
It said its shipbuilding division had completed nine vessels during the year, setting a new record for the company, although lower shipbuilding prices hurt profitability.
It also secured orders for nine vessels, including a 27,000 deadweight tonne log carrier, the company said.

Guangzhou Shipyard had completed installation of a steel girder arch for the Guangzhou Jiefang Bridge, and installation of steel box girdes and painting work on another bridge in Guangdong province, the company said.
Guangzhou Shipyard said turnover for the steel structure business had risen 170 percent year on year.
It said it had invested about 205.5 million yuan in upgrading technology, including building a 210-metre dock and upgrading its Shunde shipyard.
